about: CheckON's own output for the sample posting on the public page (frontend/src/components/Site/sample.ts), from the local stack on 2026-10-28: POST /api/v1/inspect, /refine, /answers (uses_ai_in_hiring and existing_vacancy: true), /patches/accept (all patches, pay option 2).

inspect.text:
Warehouse Shift Supervisor
Mississauga, ON · Full-time, on site

About the role
You'll lead a team of 12 on the evening shift at our distribution centre, keep orders moving and keep everyone safe.

What you'll do
• Plan the shift and assign the work
• Coach new team members
• Track productivity and safety numbers

What you bring
• 3+ years supervising in a warehouse, with Canadian experience required
• Forklift certification is an asset
• Clear communication in English

Pay and benefits
Salary: $55,000 to $110,000 a year, depending on experience.
Health and dental benefits from day one.

To apply, send your resume through our careers page.

results.message: We couldn't confirm the employer's size, so we assume it has 25 or more employees in Ontario and the job posting rules apply.
results.citation: O. Reg. 476/24, s. 1: Part III.1 of the ESA does not apply to an employer that employs fewer than 25 employees on the day the posting is posted

results.message: This is a public posting for a specific job in Ontario, so the rules apply.
results.citation: O. Reg. 476/24, s. 2 (1): a publicly advertised job posting is an external posting advertised to the general public, excluding a general recruitment campaign or help wanted sign with no specific position, a posting restricted to existing employees, and work performed outside Ontario

results.message: The posting includes the expected pay.
results.citation: ESA 2000, s. 8.2 (1): include the expected compensation or the range of expected compensation; O. Reg. 476/24, s. 2 (2): compensation means wages; s. 3: not required above $200,000 a year

results.message: The pay range is $55,000 a year wide; the limit is $50,000.

fix.guidance: Give a minimum and a maximum no more than $50,000 a year apart.

results.citation: ESA 2000, s. 8.2 (3); O. Reg. 476/24, s. 4: a range of expected compensation shall not exceed an amount equivalent to $50,000 a year; s. 3: not required above $200,000 a year

results.message: The posting doesn't say whether it is for an existing vacancy.

fix.guidance: Add a sentence saying whether this posting is for an existing vacancy.

results.citation: ESA 2000, s. 8.5 (1) (a): include a statement disclosing whether the posting is for an existing vacancy or not

results.message: Whether the posting needs an AI disclosure depends on your hiring tools.

question.text: Do you, or a recruiter acting for you, use AI to screen, assess or select applicants for this job? This includes ATS auto-ranking, resume scoring and chat screening.

results.citation: ESA 2000, s. 8.4 (1): an employer who uses artificial intelligence to screen, assess or select applicants must include a statement disclosing it; O. Reg. 476/24, s. 2 (1): definition of artificial intelligence

results.message: The posting requires Canadian experience. Ask for the skill, not where it was gained.

fix.guidance: Ask for the skill, knowledge or licence itself, and remove any condition on where experience was gained.

results.citation: ESA 2000, s. 8.3 (1): no requirements related to Canadian experience in a publicly advertised job posting or any associated application form

reminders.text: Within 45 days of an interview (or the last one), tell the applicant whether a hiring decision has been made, in person, in writing or by email, text or portal update.
reminders.citation: ESA 2000, s. 8.6; O. Reg. 476/24, s. 5: within 45 days after the interview (or the last interview), tell each interviewed applicant whether a hiring decision has been made, in person, in writing or using technology

reminders.text: Keep a copy of this posting, every revised version, any linked document and any application form for 3 years after it comes down, and what you told each interviewed applicant for 3 years.
reminders.citation: ESA 2000, s. 15 (7.1) and (7.1.1): keep a copy of every publicly advertised job posting and any associated application form for three years after public access to the posting is removed, and the information given to each interviewed applicant for three years after it was provided
